types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being. Also called Individual, Human, Man, Woman. Examples: Bill Oddie, Kate Humble, Chris Packham, Eric Idle.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: UKNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification. Examples: a registered charity, a community interest company (CIC), a benevolent society.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

types.embedding_query_text: ComedyTrio: A group of three comedians who perform together. Also called Comedy Group, Trio, Comedic Trio. Examples: The Goodies, The Goodies TV series.

chosen_type.label: ComedyTroupe
chosen_type.definition: A group of comedians who perform together.
chosen_type.justification: No exact match in schema.org, but PerformingGroup is the closest parent.

candidates.label: ComedyEvent
candidates.comment: An event featuring comedic performances or content. Also called stand-up show, humor performance, comedy festival. Examples: A stand-up comedy show, a sketch comedy performance, a comedy festival, an improv night. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: ComedyClub
candidates.comment: A local business venue primarily dedicated to hosting comedy performances. Also called stand-up club, humor venue, comedy theater. Examples: The Comedy Store, Caroline's on Broadway, Second City, The Laugh Factory. Distinct from EntertainmentBusiness, which is a broader category for businesses providing entertainment.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

types.embedding_query_text: Agent: A person who represents another person or organization. Also called Representative, Manager, Publicist. Examples: David Foster.

chosen_type.label: Attorney
chosen_type.justification: Best match among candidates for 'Agent' as a person representing another.

candidates.label: RealEstateAgent
candidates.comment: A RealEstateAgent is a LocalBusiness representing a professional who facilitates the buying, selling, or renting of properties. Also called realtor, property agent, estate agent. Examples: a residential real estate agent, a commercial property broker, a leasing agent, a real estate firm.

candidates.label: MoveAction
candidates.comment: An action where a living agent, such as a person or organization, relocates to a different place. Also called relocate, transfer residence, change location. Examples: moving to a new city, a company relocating its headquarters, a person walking to another room. Distinct from TransferAction, where the subject being moved is an inanimate object.

candidates.label: Attorney
candidates.comment: An Attorney is a LegalService professional who practices law, providing legal advice and representation. Also called lawyer, legal counsel, barrister, solicitor. Examples: a criminal defense attorney, a corporate lawyer, a family law solicitor, a public defender. Distinct from LegalService, which is the broader category of services provided by legal professionals.

candidates.label: SellAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent exchanging goods or services for money with a buyer. Also called selling, vending, trading, transacting. Examples: a store selling a product to a customer, a person selling a used car, a company selling software licenses. Distinct from BuyAction, which is the reciprocal act from the buyer's perspective.

candidates.label: DepartAction
candidates.comment: A move action representing the act of an agent leaving a specific location to travel towards a destination. Also called Leave, set off, embark, exit. Examples: A plane departing from an airport, a person leaving their home for work, a ship sailing from a port. Distinct from ArriveAction, which is the act of reaching a destination.

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A place or area. Also called Place, Area, Region, City. Examples: Rochdale, Birmingham, SCL Stadium, Wembley.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: Best match for 'Location' as it encompasses various types of places.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

types.embedding_query_text: University: An institution of higher education. Also called College, School, Institution, Academy. Examples: Cambridge University, Footlights comedy troupe.

chosen_type.label: CollegeOrUniversity
chosen_type.justification: Exact match for 'University' as an institution of higher education.

candidates.label: CollegeOrUniversity
candidates.comment: A third-level educational institution providing higher education. Also called university, college, higher education institution. Examples: Harvard University, Oxford College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Sorbonne University. Distinct from EducationalOrganization, which is a broader category for any educational body.

candidates.label: School
candidates.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: HighSchool
candidates.comment: A HighSchool is an educational organization and civic structure providing secondary education. Also called secondary school, senior high, academy. Examples: Springfield High School, Northwood Academy, a local public high school.

candidates.label: AdultEntertainment
candidates.comment: AdultEntertainment is an EntertainmentBusiness specializing in content or services intended for adults. Also called adult venue, adult club, adult establishment. Examples: A strip club, an adult movie theater, an adult bookstore.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A group of people working together for a common purpose. Also called Company, Institution, Association, Group. Examples: BBC, RSPCA, Reading FC, BBC TV.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: Best match for the general term 'Organization'.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Cooperative
candidates.comment: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A point in time. Also called Time, Point in time, Moment, Instant. Examples: 2026-07-27, 27/07/2026.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: Exact match for 'Date' as a specific point in time.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

types.embedding_query_text: TVShow Examples: Springwatch, Autumnwatch, Birding with Bill Oddie, Britain Goes Wild with Bill Oddie.

chosen_type.label: TVSeries
chosen_type.justification: Best match for 'TVShow' as it represents a series of episodes.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: TVSeries
candidates.comment: A creative work series dedicated to television broadcast and associated online delivery, comprising multiple seasons and episodes. Also called television show, TV program, broadcast series. Examples: 'Game of Thrones', 'The Office', 'Stranger Things'.

candidates.label: RadioSeason
candidates.comment: A RadioSeason is a CreativeWorkSeason dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called radio series season. Examples: Season 1 of a radio drama, a specific year's collection of a weekly radio show, a themed season of a podcast broadcast on radio.

candidates.label: TVEpisode
candidates.comment: A single installment of a television series, typically part of a season. Also called television episode, show episode, broadcast installment. Examples: 'The Pilot' episode of a new series, 'Episode 5 of Season 2' of a drama.

types.embedding_query_text: Song Examples: The Funky Gibbon, The Inbetweenies.

chosen_type.label: MusicRecording
chosen_type.justification: Best match for 'Song' as a recorded musical composition.

candidates.label: MusicAlbum
candidates.comment: A MusicAlbum, as a MusicPlaylist, is a collection of music tracks released together. Also called album, record album, studio album. Examples: 'Thriller' by Michael Jackson, 'Abbey Road' by The Beatles, a compilation album. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is usually a single song.

candidates.label: MusicAlbumProductionType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumProductionType is an enumeration classifying a music album by its content type. Also called album type, production category. Examples: StudioAlbum, LiveAlbum, Soundtrack, CompilationAlbum. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the release format.

candidates.label: MusicAlbumReleaseType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumReleaseType is an enumeration describing the kind of release for a music album. Also called release format, album release category. Examples: Single, EP, Album. Distinct from MusicAlbumProductionType, which describes the content type.

candidates.label: MusicRecording
candidates.comment: A MusicRecording, as a CreativeWork, is a recorded performance of a musical composition, usually a single song. Also called music track, song recording, audio track. Examples: 'Yesterday' by The Beatles (the recorded version), a single from an album, a demo track. Distinct from MusicComposition, which is the abstract musical work.

candidates.label: MusicVideoObject
candidates.comment: A MusicVideoObject, as a MediaObject, is a video file primarily featuring a musical performance or accompanying a song. Also called music video, song video, official video. Examples: 'Thriller' music video by Michael Jackson, a Vevo music video, a live performance video. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a segment of a film.

types.embedding_query_text: ComedyTroupe Examples: Footlights comedy troupe, Monty Python.

chosen_type.label: ComedyTroupe
chosen_type.definition: A group of comedians who perform together.
chosen_type.justification: Similar to E2, no exact match, but PerformingGroup is the closest parent.

candidates.label: ComedyEvent
candidates.comment: An event featuring comedic performances or content. Also called stand-up show, humor performance, comedy festival. Examples: A stand-up comedy show, a sketch comedy performance, a comedy festival, an improv night. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: ComedyClub
candidates.comment: A local business venue primarily dedicated to hosting comedy performances. Also called stand-up club, humor venue, comedy theater. Examples: The Comedy Store, Caroline's on Broadway, Second City, The Laugh Factory. Distinct from EntertainmentBusiness, which is a broader category for businesses providing entertainment.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: DanceGroup

Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

chosen_type.label: SportsTeam
chosen_type.justification: Exact match for 'SportsTeam' as a group of athletes competing together.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SportsClub
candidates.comment: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: TennisComplex
candidates.comment: A local business or sports activity location featuring multiple tennis courts and related facilities. Also called tennis center, tennis club, tennis facility. Examples: 'Indian Wells Tennis Garden', a community tennis complex, a private tennis club.

chosen_type.label: RadioStation
chosen_type.justification: Exact match for 'RadioStation' as an organization broadcasting radio content.

candidates.label: RadioStation
candidates.comment: A RadioStation is a LocalBusiness representing an organization that broadcasts radio content. Also called radio broadcaster, radio company. Examples: WNYC, BBC Radio, a local commercial radio station, a public radio station.

candidates.label: RadioSeries
candidates.comment: A RadioSeries is a CreativeWorkSeries dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called radio show, radio program series. Examples: "The Archers", "This American Life", a long-running radio drama, a daily news radio program.

candidates.label: RadioSeason
candidates.comment: A RadioSeason is a CreativeWorkSeason dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called radio series season. Examples: Season 1 of a radio drama, a specific year's collection of a weekly radio show, a themed season of a podcast broadcast on radio.

candidates.label: RadioChannel
candidates.comment: A RadioChannel is a BroadcastChannel representing a unique instance of a radio BroadcastService on a CableOrSatelliteService lineup. Also called radio frequency, radio station channel. Examples: 98.7 FM, SiriusXM Channel 100, a specific digital radio channel, a local AM station.

candidates.label: RadioClip
candidates.comment: A RadioClip is a Clip representing a short radio program or a segment of a radio program. Also called radio segment, audio clip, radio excerpt. Examples: a news report from a radio show, a short interview clip, a commercial break, a song played on the radio.

types.embedding_query_text: RadioShow Examples: The World At One.

candidates.label: RadioSeason
candidates.comment: A RadioSeason is a CreativeWorkSeason dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called radio series season. Examples: Season 1 of a radio drama, a specific year's collection of a weekly radio show, a themed season of a podcast broadcast on radio.

candidates.label: RadioSeries
candidates.comment: A RadioSeries is a CreativeWorkSeries dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called radio show, radio program series. Examples: "The Archers", "This American Life", a long-running radio drama, a daily news radio program.

candidates.label: RadioStation
candidates.comment: A RadioStation is a LocalBusiness representing an organization that broadcasts radio content. Also called radio broadcaster, radio company. Examples: WNYC, BBC Radio, a local commercial radio station, a public radio station.

candidates.label: RadioClip
candidates.comment: A RadioClip is a Clip representing a short radio program or a segment of a radio program. Also called radio segment, audio clip, radio excerpt. Examples: a news report from a radio show, a short interview clip, a commercial break, a song played on the radio.

candidates.label: RadioEpisode
candidates.comment: A RadioEpisode is an Episode representing a single installment of a radio series or season. Also called radio show episode, audio episode. Examples: an episode of "This American Life", a specific installment of a radio drama, a segment of a daily news program.

chosen_type.label: SocialMediaPlatform
chosen_type.definition: An online platform for creating and sharing content with social networking features
chosen_type.justification: No exact match in schema.org, but DigitalPlatformEnumeration is related.

candidates.label: SocialMediaPosting
candidates.comment: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.

candidates.label: DiscussionForumPosting
candidates.comment: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Examples: A question posted on a tech support forum, a comment in a gaming community thread, a new topic started on a hobby board. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically a longer, standalone article on a blog.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: BlogPosting
candidates.comment: An Article that is an individual entry or post published within a blog. Also called blog post, blog entry, weblog post. Examples: "A blog post about new software features", "An article on a travel blog", "A recipe post on a food blog". Distinct from Blog, which is the collection of posts.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.
